questions.q: What accusation does Yahweh make against the shepherds of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh accuses the shepherds of Israel of not shepherding at all, but of slaughtering the best animals of the flock.

questions.q: How did the shepherds of Israel rule over the flock?
questions.a: The shepherds of Israel ruled over the flock with strength and violence.

questions.q: What then happened to the flock?
questions.a: The flock was then scattered and became food for all the living beasts in the fields.

questions.q: Who were the shepherds of Israel actually guarding?
questions.a: The shepherds of Israel were actually guarding themselves.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the shepherds of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will dismiss the shepherds of Israel and take away the flock from their mouths.

questions.q: From where does Yahweh say he will gather his flock?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on the day of clouds and darkness. Then he will bring them out from among the peoples, he will gather them from the lands.

questions.q: How does Yahweh say he will shepherd?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will shepherd with justice.

questions.q: Among what three groups does Yahweh say he will judge?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will judge among the sheep, rams, and goats.

questions.q: What has been done to the weak and thin sheep?
questions.a: The weak and thin sheep have been pushed and gored until they have been scattered.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh say he will raise up to shepherd the flock?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will raise up his servant David to shepherd the flock.

questions.q: When Yahweh raises up his shepherd, what will Yahweh do so the sheep will live securely?
questions.a: Yahweh will make a covenant of peace with the sheep and remove the evil wild animals from the land.

questions.q: What will the nations no longer be able to do to the sheep?
questions.a: The nations will no longer be able to plunder the sheep or bring insults against them.

questions.q: What will the house of Israel then know?
questions.a: The house of Israel will then know that Yahweh their God is with them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh declare to the sheep, the house of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh declares that he is the God of the house of Israel, and that they are his people.

commentary.text: The rulers reproved. (Ezek. 34:1-6) The people are to be restored to their own land. (Ezek. 34:7-16) The kingdom of Christ. (Ezek. 34:17-31)

Ezek. 34:1-6 The people became as sheep without a shepherd, were given up as a prey to their enemies, and the land was utterly desolated. No rank or office can exempt from the reproofs of God's word, men who neglect their duty, and abuse the trust reposed in them.

Ezek. 34:7-16 The Lord declared that he intended mercy towards the scattered flock. Doubtless this, in the first place, had reference to the restoration of the Jews. It also represented the good Shepherd's tender care of the souls of his people. He finds them in their days of darkness and ignorance, and brings them to his fold. He comes to their relief in times of persecution and temptation. He leads them in the ways of righteousness, and causes them to rest on his love and faithfulness. The proud and self-sufficient, are enemies of the true gospel and of believers; against such we must guard. He has rest for disquieted saints, and terror for presumptuous sinners.

Ezek. 34:17-31 The whole nation seemed to be the Lord's flock, yet they were very different characters; but he knew how to distinguish between them. By good pastures and deep waters, are meant the pure word of God and the dispensing of justice. The latter verses, 23-31, prophesy of Christ, and of the most glorious times of his church on earth. Under Him, as the good Shepherd, the church would be a blessing to all around. Christ, though excellent in himself, was as a tender plant out of a dry ground. Being the Tree of life, bearing all the fruits of salvation, he yields spiritual food to the souls of his people. Our constant desire and prayer should be, that there may be showers of blessings in every place where the truth of Christ is preached; and that all who profess the gospel may be filled with fruits of righteousness.
